title: Detecting Cash-out Users via Dense Subgraphs

problem.claim: Detect fraudulent cash-out users using only personal credit card data from banks.

gap.claim: Existing graph-based methods mainly target online payment activities and rely on large amounts of online user data, making them unsuitable for traditional credit card services in commercial banks.

contributions.claim: Formulates cash-out detection as identifying dense blocks to address scarce labeled data.
Defines a bipartite multigraph for user-merchant transactions and formalizes cash-out behavior from time, capital, cyclicity, and topotaxy perspectives.
Develops ANTICO, using suspicious-activity metrics and a greedy algorithm to identify suspicious blocks by metric optimization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Theoretical analysis reports a provable upper bound for ANTICO's effectiveness in detecting cash-out users.
Experiments report that ANTICO outperforms state-of-the-art methods on synthetic and real-world banking data for accurately detecting cash-out users.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines cash-out fraud as illegitimate merchant payments used to withdraw cash from a credit card.
Describes feature-engineered classifiers and graph-based approaches for cash-out detection.
Identifies the limited suitability of existing graph methods for traditional bank credit card services.
Introduces dense-block detection using a transaction multigraph, behavioral definitions, and ANTICO.
Reports theoretical and experimental results for ANTICO.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, sample sizes, baseline identities, or quantitative performance margins.
